title: d-3: dependency-qualification
description:
## Deliverables
1. Perform the complete changed-registry dependency sweep across root, template and separate-consumer inputs: replace exact/tilde pins, bare versions and carets with >= tested floors and no upper bound, update rmcp to patched >=3.9, preserve features, adapt source/API call sites and qualify Windows/Monty under the supported toolchains — REQ-RUN-0002/0005; NFR-RUN-0007; ANC-012/037.
2. Update sc-config/sc-transport/sc-runtime READMEs alongside changed API/dependency behavior; preserve documented test-util helper and synchronous sc-config scope — REQ-RUN-0702; NFR-CFG-0002; NFR-RT-0001.

3. Own pin removal in crates/sc-command/Cargo.toml and crates/sc-runtime/Cargo.toml (normal/dev lines), template/crates/daemon/Cargo*.toml and tests/contracts/phase-c/application-control/Cargo.toml: rmcp >=3.9, utoipa >=6.0.0, utoipa-axum >=0.3.0. Preserve the unpublished compile-fail fixture crates/sc-runtime/tests/fixtures/utoipa5-router/Cargo.toml with incompatible utoipa-axum ^0.2.0; it is test input, not a published SDK or template dependency. Preserve feature flags and its negative assertion — ANC-037.

4. Implement the one check_dependency_manifests(paths) and its unit tests in tests/unit/generation/test_runtime_ecosystem_upgrade.py: SDK-owned registry defaults use >= tested floors with no upper bound (ANC-037). Inputs are explicit manifest paths; d-11 supplies generated manifests and d-12 unpacked archives. Keep this interim under ADR-RUN-0005 until equivalent sc-lint#936 enforcement is shipped and adopted.

## Boundaries and handoffs
No storage engine, cron implementation, generated wiring or registry release is closed here. d-5 owns shared root Cargo/version/lock/boundary edits, d-6 backend dependencies, d-9 cron dependencies; d-3 owns the command manifest together with compiled server/schema compatibility; d-10 consumes that code and adds storage helpers after it. Qualified source is consumed by d-12; d-11 independently tests generated integration.
In the complete command manifest convert every registry requirement, including dev/optional entries, to open floors: rmcp >=3.9, utoipa >=6.0.0, schemars >=1.2.3, sc-observability-types >=1.5.0, axum >=0.8.9 and serde/serde_json/tokio >=1. Preserve features. This lands with the normal server/schema conversions and typed public error/envelope ABI compiled against those identities; d-10 consumes that code before adding storage helpers (ANC-037).
design:
Open registry floors and tested recommendations (ANC-037/038):

Every registry dependency requirement in published crates and templates uses >= a tested floor with no upper bound, including SDK dependencies. Convert bare-version and caret requirements as well as exact/tilde pins. Consumers may pin any versions in their own manifests or lockfiles. The release recommends its tested combination instead of restricting consumer choices (owner m6 extension; ANC-037). Preserve existing dependency features.

Rusqlite qualification and its one manifest owner are d-6; this sprint does not repeat that work.

Monty and monty-types remain optional and use >=1.4.0. The normal suite tests the selected versions on the documented toolchain. Intentional non-shipped negative fixtures retain their incompatible identity; they do not constrain consumers.


Closure note: integration applies to this complete independent feature, even in the first wave; its actual API/toolchain interactions and executable acceptance close here, not an unimplemented contract.
Own complete sc-command and template daemon manifest rmcp changes here; no d-5 parallel edits. Workspace remains development0.2.0; only d-12 bumps final coordinated0.3.0. d-10 consumes this manifest and follows d-3 to add sc-storage later. D-5 common command traits live in sc-storage, so this sprint needs no new storage dependency to close. Native check uses cargo tree; umbrella SQLx mixed feature conflict is handled by d-7/8 direct crates and fully integrated in d-11.
Own source compatibility adaptations and the callable manifest checker; d-3 owns the command manifest and matching rmcp3.9 server/schema conversions; d-10 consumes that compiled code, not just a same-file permission. Shared contract registry files remain d-5-owned.
acceptance_criteria:
req:REQ-RUN-0002/compatibility — Every registry requirement written in owned published/template manifests is >= its tested floor with no upper bound (ANC-037). Preserve optional features and existing unpublished negative compile fixtures. Consumers may pin their own manifests and lockfiles; run the normal test suite.
req:REQ-RUN-0005/source — rmcp>=3.9 builds/tests with existing command/server/schema paths; selected Windows/Monty jobs run on the supported toolchains. No sc-compose or ATM production dependency. Public0.3.0 docs describe actual crate behavior and unchanged sc-config sync API. Phase D retains the existing sc_command::observability shim; normal observability tests cover the fixed noop ServiceName literal with the selected types, without an exact pin or registry-availability/signature probe (ADR-RUN-0017; REQ-RUN-0309).
Required commands: just lint; just test; cargo build --workspace; sc-lint lint sc-boundary --root . --config sc-lint.toml. Document ordinary commands/prerequisites in docs/development/dependency-upgrades.md. No separate dependency endpoint CI or probes; no registry publication or full storage feature claimed.
Cargo workspace build and normal tests pass in this sprint own branch at closure; no unowned manifest change is assumed. Root source/dependency compatibility behavior is req:REQ-RUN-0002/source-ranges; registry/publication behavior only d-12. Cargo.lock is not native-identity evidence.
req:REQ-RUN-0002/manifest-policy — The one checker tests accepted open-floor and rejected restrictive SDK defaults, checks this sprint's owned manifests and is called by generation/release consumers. Consumer-owned pins are outside this rule (ANC-037).

dependencies.title: Phase D: shared app storage, channel writer and published consumer migration
dependencies.description:
Phase D makes the SDK easy to adopt and lets consumers choose dependency upgrades. Product intent is PRD v2.0; the release is the owner-selected eight public crates at0.3.0. Generic backends contain no consumer table code. Sprint metadata.owned_paths is the authoritative full file fence; summaries below are navigation only.

| Sprint | Wave | Boundary | Consumed artifacts |
|---|---|---|---|
| d-3 | 1 | dependency/source compatibility | none; owns the one manifest checker |
| d-4 | 1 | generation tooling | none |
| d-5 | 1 | storage/atomic/row contract | none; owner ratification and Active ADR0020/0021 before consumers |
| d-6 | 2 | SQLite backend | d-5 production contract |
| d-7 | 2 | Postgres backend | d-5 production contract |
| d-8 | 2 | MySQL backend | d-5 production contract |
| d-9 | 2 | cron domain adapter | d-5 production contract and additive legacy build |
| d-10 | 2 | common commands/transforms | d-3 compiled command server/schema/error ABI, d-5 Storage/row contract |
| d-11 | 3 | generated composition | d-3 checker, d-4 tools, d-6/7/8/9/10 code |
| d-12 | 3 | registry migration/release/recommendations | d-3 source/checker, d-4 tools, d-6/9/10 code; d-11 completion checked before upload |

Ten sprints; critical path3, width6. No dependency exists solely because two sprints edit the same manifest. The release and generated-integration sprints prepare in parallel; upload waits for completed generated integration. No implementation dispatch before plan approval.
dependencies.design:
PRD v2.0 governs product scope. sc-storage is std-only; storage/atomic/row traits are the shared contract, with only transaction name/mode properties. SQLite uses one async queue and one writer thread exclusively owning its sole write-mode connection, queued writes commit together, and replies follow commit. Only the writer runtime uses Runtime::block_on. Readers use blocking_recv without a runtime; async callers never block or use spawn_blocking to submit writes. Consumer rows/schema/migrations stay above generic engines. sc-cron implements its policy once over generic atomic Storage<CronRow> and keeps raw backend mutation out of the CronStore public facade.

D-5 owns contract types, shared registry/boundary definitions, required REQ/ADR amendments and the minimal legacy compatibility build. Its layer-file handoffs are additive contract/legacy artifacts on existing dependencies, not simultaneous same-wave edits. d-9 owns the0.3.0 removal of ScheduleStore/SqliteScheduleStore and obsolete SQLite files after those artifacts compile. Root Cargo.toml passes directly from d-5 registrations to d-12 release-version conversion; d-6 reads it. d-3 owns the command manifest with its rmcp3.9 server/schema compatibility code; d-10 consumes that compiled artifact and later adds storage helpers. Specific crate facade boundaries pass from d-5 to their implementation owner on the existing must-follow edges.

D-5 owner ratification is pending and gates its closure; ADR0020/0021 must be Active before d-6..d-12 start. The actual no-panic rule sc-lint#931 and transaction-safe analyzer remain required for affected owner-sprint closure and are rechecked before publication. Lead owns the external analyzer request; missing delivery is a real blocker, not a waiver.

D-3 owns the sole interim SDK manifest checker; d-11 invokes it on generated outputs and d-12 on exact archives/upload. Remove it after equivalent sc-lint#936 release/adoption. Published/template registry requirements are open tested floors (ANC-037); normal tests check the selected versions, with no dedicated min/latest jobs. Consumers may pin what they want. D-12 alone produces the final newest-tested Cargo.lock recommendation and matching .sc-runtime/tested-dependencies.json (ANC-038).

Eight published packages at0.3.0: sc-storage, sc-runtime-db-sqlite, sc-config, sc-transport, sc-command, sc-runtime, sc-cron, sc-cron-commands. Postgres/MySQL generic engines remain generated this phase under that approved packaging scope; their implementation fixes need template updates/regeneration, explicitly recorded in ADR0020. They do not acquire an invented library-upgrade guarantee. D-12 derives publication order from actual manifests, sc-storage first, rehearses exact archives, then proves actual upstream beads-cache PR open/CI green against registry crates. Its independent preparation does not upload until d-11 sanity is closed and completed composition merged, with ratification and actual safety rules passing. Missing release predicates leave publication open.

The phase is one append-only stack with one writer. Metadata layer is planned presentation order; actual link order follows completion. pr_target is the consumed lower bound, not false sibling serialization. Canonical root Cargo.lock is d-12-owned. Historical probe facts remain in Git/review evidence, not a second live scope document.


## Boundary map and generated targets
Read existing boundaries/<crate>/<crate>.toml. sc-config dependencies serde/serde_json unchanged; sc-transport tokio/reqwest/serde->sc-runtime unchanged; sc-command gains sc-storage, consumers sc-cron/sc-cron-commands/sc-runtime; sc-runtime composes transport/command, no storage trait placement there; sc-cron loses direct SQLite backend, depends on sc-storage/sc-command; sc-cron-commands adapts scheduler. Generic writer dependencies sc-storage/rusqlite/Tokio only, NEVER sc-cron/ATM/sc-compose; no consumer SQL/schema. New boundaries/sc-storage/sc-storage.toml has no sc-* dependency. Generated store/service boundaries are emitted by template/boundaries/render.py at boundaries/<prefixed-package>/<prefixed-package>.toml with existing Store/Stores facades; no invented static template boundaries. Application row descriptors/migrations are supplied at open, engine applies them before exposing store.
dependencies.acceptance_criteria:
1. d-11 closes actual generated SQLite app/cron shared database/channel writer, real typed transforms/CRUD and all selected engines/mixed layouts; no vulnerable SQLx SQLite or separate cron.db default, no fake engine proof.
2. d-12 closes actual upstream migration PR open/CI-green at exact SHA against eight published0.3.0 crates; no path/patch/Git SDK substitute. All source/package/API/docs and normal test suites pass.
3. Generic backends contain no consumer table code; named owned retryable atomic API and static+runtime safety checks actually operate. Public changed storage APIs return typed errors/no panic; writer panic fails every waiting caller. External rule and ratification blockers stay explicit until met.
4. All existing workspace/lint/test/boundary/publishing-kit/controlled-host benchmark gates pass; publication waits for closed d-11 sanity and owner ratification, after exact archive rehearsal. Required coverage and independent plan/development gates are separate from schema validation.
